name: TurboVec — Vector Quantization for RAG Memory Compression

score.rationale: Mature compression algorithm with proven 8× ratio on embedding indexes. However, C9 has no RAG layer yet, making this premature infrastructure.

layer_rationale: Speculative but grounded. Vector quantization is established information theory. Application to AI memory is validated by Google at scale.

cluster_mapping.3: Quantum Information & Complexity — Quantization is a form of lossy compression that preserves semantic structure. Analogous to coarse-graining in statistical mechanics.
cluster_mapping.6: Neuromorphic Computing — Reduces RAM footprint of embedding indexes from ~60GB to ~4GB, enabling phone-scale semantic retrieval.

tech_profile.speed: Faster than FAISS, zero training, fully offline

tier_1.name: Documentation & Entry
tier_1.description: Formal entry created. No local deployment.

tier_2.name: RAG Layer Prototype
tier_2.description: When C9 adds semantic retrieval over 7,276 files + The Well papers + TNG docs, TurboVec compresses the embedding index to fit on phone RAM.

tier_3.name: Production Integration
tier_3.description: Replace FAISS/naive vector stores with TurboVec-backed index in c9_knowledge_retriever.py

references: arXiv:2507.04575 — TurboQuant: 31 GB of AI Memory to 4 GB
